text.p: British retailer Storehouse Plc is forecast to report around an eight percent profit increase with its annual results next Thursday, but recent share price weakness has pointed to worries about current sales, analysts said.

Retail analysts are predicting pre-tax profits for the year to end March of between 118 million and 121 million stg against 109.9 million a year earlier. The dividend is expected to rise to about 8.3 pence from 7.2.

Analysts are waiting for the results and an update on trading since the end of March to confirm or counter perceptions that the firm's two retail brands Bhs and Mothercare have been performing below expectations since Christmas.
A weak market for childrens clothes has prompted fears for Mothercare's sales, but there have also been worries about Bhs.
Forecasts point to about an eight percent sales increase at Bhs and a 1.6 percent gain at Mothercare, analysts said.
Storehouse's shares are trading near their lowest for 2-1/2 years, weighed down by worries that the upcoming results could fall short of expectations.
The shares were up 1 1/2p at 208 pence by 0810 GMT.
In January, Storehouse reported a nine percent sales increase in the six weeks to December 24, although it said Mothercare was disappointing.
The group has bounced back from problems caused by over-extending itself in the 1980s, but over the past year the recovery seems to have lost momentum, analysts said.
The group also has a franchise business, which is expanding rapidly overseas.
